thread:
Rahul: Quick FYI — during the canary we captured some debug logs that include fragments of KV cache keys. Not full tokens but looks sensitive. Need a quick scope: what was in logs, which orgs might be impacted, who can delete archives, and whether Legal/comms should be looped. @Kim @Jenny

Kim: On it. Can you paste an example (sanitized) and where the logs live (ELK, S3, CloudWatch)? Which service was running the canary?

Rahul: Sanitized snippet below. Logs landed in staging ELK archive (s3) and transient CloudWatch for ~48h. Service: runtime-router v3.2-canary.

```
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z DEBUG kv_fetch key=cache:usr_abc123:kv_part="eyJhbGci..." path=/models/gpt-3
```

Jenny: That base64-ish chunk could be part of a short-lived token fragment. Not a full scoped token in itself, but still sensitive. I'll grep to get counts. Running: `grep -R "cache:usr_" /var/logs/canary | wc -l`

Carla: Just to confirm — this is staging canary only, not prod, right?

Rahul: Correct — canary routing only. Caveat: some internal test users are mapped to customer orgs; need to check those mappings.

Kim: I can run an ELK query for the time window and return affected org_ids. If it's small (<5 orgs) we do targeted outreach; if larger, escalate to wider comms.

SecBot: Automated policy note: rotate any short-lived keys if exposure is confirmed. See policy: incident-rotations v2.

Jenny: Quick results: 3 unique org_ids found: redwood-dev, acme-int, beta-co. Total 12 matching log lines during the canary window. No prod indices touched.

Carla: Any PII in those lines? From snippet it looks like cache key fragments and model paths, not prompts.

Rahul: No user prompts or raw messages in the lines we saw. The cache key includes internal user id and a base64 fragment — could be considered customer data. I recommend we notify the affected orgs and offer rotation support.

Kim: Drafting comms. Proposed actions: 1) delete archives for the time window, 2) rotate short-lived keys tied to canary mappings, 3) confirm prod unaffected, 4) targeted DM to affected orgs with offer to rotate, 5) internal postmortem if customers are contacted. @Liz / Legal please advise.

Liz: Thanks for the tag. From the initial scope this looks like limited exposure of internal identifiers and token fragments in staging. Recommend we notify the three affected orgs with neutral language and offer assistance rotating any keys. No need for a public disclosure. Approve the draft once Ops confirms deletion and rotation.

OpsOncall: I'll take rotation of service-level short-lived keys and update within 1h. Will post confirmation here.

Jenny: Archive deletion scheduled and executed for 2026-03-22 14:00-14:30 window. CloudWatch streams for the canary cleared and retention set to expire immediately for those streams. Commands used: `aws s3 rm s3://redwood-elk-archive/canary/2026-03-22 --recursive` and `aws logs delete-log-stream --log-group-name /canary/runtime-router --log-stream-name canary-2026-03-22`

Rahul: Thanks team. Kim please finish the comms draft and tag Legal for a quick sign-off. If anything customer-facing is needed we'll open a short postmortem doc.

Kim: Drafted message and posted in #incidents-drafts. Plan: targeted DM to the three orgs, offer rotation support, explain no prompts or prod data exposed. Will await Liz sign-off then send. No public status page update planned.

Liz: Approved language. Legal does not require press notification. Keep an internal postmortem and record actions for compliance.

Rahul: :thumbsup: Good work. Closing async triage here — will open postmortem only if a customer requests escalation.

OpsOncall: Rotation completed and verified. Confirmed deletion of archives and cloudwatch streams. All actions done, closing loop.

Jenny: Final note: added a short guard in runtime-router to sanitize KV keys before logging (PR open: github.com/redwood/runtime-router/pull/412).

Rahul: Great — thanks everyone.
